100.title: Please tell us if any of the following apply to you.

redFlags.text: Unsteady walking, loss of balance, or sudden difficulty staying upright.
Sudden loss of bowel or bladder control, leaking urine, or inability to pass urine.
Dropping objects frequently or struggling with fine finger tasks like buttoning shirts or turning keys.
Uncontrolled muscle twitching, jumping, or sudden spasms in your arms or legs.
Frequent tripping or feeling like your feet catch on the floor when walking.
Rapid, rhythmic, uncontrollable shaking in your foot or ankle when resting.
Sudden weakness when twisting jar lids or turning doorknobs.
Hand feels heavy, clumsy, or unable to make a tight fist.
Numbness, tingling, or pins-and-needles spreading through your whole hand or fingers.
Noticeable weakness in an entire arm or leg.
Unusual heaviness in both legs while walking.
Overall muscle strength getting steadily worse over days or weeks.
Arm weakness getting steadily worse over time.
Numbness or weakness that is severe or rapidly spreading.
Severe pain that never stops, even when resting or taking over-the-counter pain relievers.
Fever or chills alongside your shoulder or neck pain.
Drenching night sweats.
Unexplained weight loss without dieting.
Weakened immune system (due to illness, chemotherapy, or immunosuppressive medication).
Constant, intense pain that stays severe even when lying completely flat.
Sharp pain when pressing directly on the bones of your spine.
Pain, numbness, or weakness shooting from neck into arm right after a fall or accident.
Sharp bone pain or grinding directly over your collarbone when moving your arm.
Inability to move arm after a hard blow or fall onto shoulder blade.
A popping or tearing feeling near shoulder blade during an injury, followed by inability to lift arm.
Hand or arm turns pale, cold, or bluish when lifting your arm overhead or reaching backward.
Tingling or numbness in arm overhead, combined with cold hands or skin color changes.
Hand weakness combined with a droopy eyelid or smaller pupil on the same side of your face.
Symptoms (numbness, pain, or weakness) affecting both arms or legs simultaneously.
Widespread pain, numbness, and weakness across neck, shoulder blade, arm, and hand after an injury.
History of cancer.
Recent severe fall, car accident, or direct high-impact injury.
Severe pain when pressing on a specific bone in shoulder or upper back.
Visible bump, gap, or sudden structural change in collarbone, shoulder, or neck.

200.title: Neck vs. Shoulder Origin
200.questionText: Does neck movement send pain down your arm?
200.patientText: Does tilting your head backward or turning your neck toward your sore side cause sharp pain, numbness, or tingling to shoot down your arm?

options.label: Yes, neck movement sends pain or numbness down my arm.
No, neck movement does not send pain down my arm.

210.title: Pain Location and Spread
210.questionText: Where do you feel the pain, and where does it spread?

options.label: Pain starts in the neck and spreads past the elbow, with weakness, numbness, or loss of feeling.
Pain stays at outer shoulder, top of shoulder, or front of upper arm, and does not pass elbow.

220.title: Night Pain
220.questionText: Does pain wake you at night or disturb your sleep?

options.label: Yes, I have pain at night or my sleep is disturbed.
No, I do not have night pain.

300.title: Neck origin favored
300.primaryDiagnosis: Symptoms indicate nerve irritation originating in the neck (cervical radiculopathy). Requires neck-focused evaluation.

400.title: Shoulder origin favored
400.primaryDiagnosis: Symptoms indicate pain originating inside the shoulder joint.

500.title: Origin indeterminate
500.primaryDiagnosis: Symptoms do not clearly isolate neck or shoulder origin. Medical or physiotherapy evaluation recommended before structured shoulder exercise.

999.title: Urgent Medical Care Required
999.primaryDiagnosis: You have selected a red flag symptom that requires medical evaluation before starting any self-directed physiotherapy exercises.
